# `Scanner/Resolve-v0` · The fastest scan that separates a detail

**B · Spatial encoding and reconstruction** · Fourier encoding · kind 2, set · isolates B10: Matrix, pixel and voxel: resolution is the extent of k-space. [The map](../../docs/tasks.md)

**Status:** CANDIDATE: the gate has not been run (no stored result)

The pixel follows from the detail. Three pairs of small bright features sit in signal-free inserts of a gel phantom; the spacing of each pair is hidden. The agent looks (a localiser costs scan time), measures the spacings and the size of the object, and prescribes for each pair the spin-echo scan with the coarsest pixel that still separates it. A pixel as large as the spacing does not: the point-spread function is a sinc.

Kind of task: **undetermined** (no stored gate result).

```python
import mrgym
env = mrgym.make("Scanner/Resolve-v0", level=2, seed=0)
obs, info = env.reset()
obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step({"name": "scanner_info", "arguments": {}})
```

| Given | Deliver | Scored by |
|---|---|---|
| A test object with three pairs of small features at hidden spacings; the scanner; 15.5 s of scan time for looking | Per pair, the geometry of a spin-echo scan: phase-encode axis, field of view, phase field of view, matrix | Re-scan on the hidden object: whole object inside, the pair separated (dip of at least one half between the two peaks), an SNR floor, a scan-time cap, scan time within 20 % of the fastest such geometry |

## World

- On the table: QA phantom (an elliptical disc of gel), three signal-free inserts with a pair of bright discs each, 1.5 T
- Sequences that matter here: spgr, se
- Formulas the agent is given: pixel = fov_mm / matrix along both axes; lines = matrix x phase_fov; scan time = overhead + TR x (1 + lines); the image of a point is sinc(x / pixel): two points merge at a spacing of one pixel and show a dip of one half at 1.63 pixels; pixel i of n is centred at (i - n / 2) x pixel

| Hidden (measurable only by scanning) | Told |
|---|---|
| spacing and position of the two features of each pair | the target sequence |
| size of the object, and at level 3 its orientation | the marked regions (a circle around each pair, a reference circle in the gel) |
| its materials | the pass rule: dip, SNR floor, time cap, time factor |
| fields and system state | the instrument datasheet |
| noise level | realised protocol, timing, limits and cost of every plan and scan |
| the 128-bit world seed | any stored image, and the numbers along any line through it |

## Deliverable and reward

- Deliverable: `submit` with `{'<pair id>': {'pe_dir': 'y | x', 'fov_mm': '<mm>', 'phase_fov': '<fraction>', 'matrix': '<even integer>'}}`
- Reward range [0.0, 1.0]; paid only at submit; 0 on every other step
- Gates: the scanner log replays and is within budget; at least one accepted scan; the console accepts each geometry; the whole object lies inside the image (hidden outline, 0.5 mm slack); dip between the two features >= 0.5 on the noise-free image read between its pixels; SNR of the reference region >= 12 (noise-free signal over the analytic noise); scan time <= 60 s; scan time <= 1.2 x the scan time of the fastest geometry that passes the gates above (search on the hidden world)
- Error: `largest over the pairs of T / T_opt - 1: scan time of the delivered geometry over the oracle's optimum`
- Score: `none: the reward is 1 for a pass and 0 otherwise`
- Passing: all gates, for every pair

## Gate: the control policies on fresh instances

**Gate not stored on this engine** (`mrgym-engine-0.2.0`). `mrgym gate Scanner/Resolve-v0 --n 300 --write` measures and stores it.

| Policy | Must | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `reference` | pass | one 1 mm localiser; spacing of each pair from the two peaks of a profile; pixel = 0.55 x spacing; smallest field of view that holds the object |
| `prior` | fail | no scan; a geometry that holds any object, with a pixel of 2 mm |
| `console_default` | fail | one token scan, then the console's default field of view and matrix |
| `fixed_recipe` | fail | one token scan, then one constant geometry (axis, pixel, lines) for every pair, tuned on other worlds |
| `sweep` | fail | scans at a fixed list of pixels and delivers the coarsest at which its own image shows two peaks |
| `wrong_units` | fail | the reference's geometry with the field of view in centimetres |
| `pixel_is_spacing` | ablation | the reference with the pixel set to the measured spacing |
| `fixed_axis` | ablation | the reference with the phase-encode axis always along y |
| `half_spacing` | reported | the reference with the pixel set to half the measured spacing |
| `open_loop` | reported | a fixed scan list and a fixed estimator: the reference itself (no scan depends on a measurement) |

## What the agent reads at reset (level 2, seed 0)

~~~text
# Prescribe the fastest scan that separates each marked pair of features
A test object lies in the scanner: an elongated disc of gel with three signal-free inserts, centred on the isocentre to
within 2 mm. Each insert holds a pair of small bright features. The long axis of the object lies along x,
and so does the line through the two features of each pair.
For each pair the examination needs one spin-echo image of the whole object in which the two features are separate:
    sequence se, tr_ms 500, te_ms at the console minimum, bandwidth_hz_per_px 300, 1 average, slice 5 mm,
    field of view centred on the isocentre, not rotated, all of k-space sampled.
Regions (circles; centre and radius in mm from the isocentre; A, B and C each hold one pair, REF lies in the gel):
  A: y 4.3, x 55.4, radius 11
  B: y -3.2, x -51.7, radius 11
  C: y -5.6, x 1.3, radius 11
  REF: y 38.8, x 26.2, radius 8
Deliver one geometry per pair (A, B, C) with `submit`: the phase-encode axis (`pe_dir`), the readout field of view
(`fov_mm`), `phase_fov` (the phase field of view as a fraction of `fov_mm`) and `matrix`. The pixel is fov_mm / matrix
along both axes. The target scans are not run in this episode: the scanner evaluates the geometries you deliver.
Your own scans may use any sequence and any parameters the console accepts; only the deliverable is evaluated, on the scan the task names.
That scan is not charged to the scan-time budget and not limited by it.
The size of the object and the spacing of each pair are not known in advance.

Passing, for each pair, on the scan with the geometry you delivered for it:
  the whole object lies inside the image (so nothing wraps around);
  the two features are separated: along the line through their centres the image falls, between its two peaks, to at
  most 50 % of the lower peak (read on the image interpolated between its pixels, so it does not matter where
  the pixel centres fall);
  the signal-to-noise ratio of region REF is at least 12;
  the scan takes at most 60 s;
  the scan takes at most 20 % longer than the fastest geometry that meets the four requirements above.
The scanner's log must show that you measured. A length in the wrong unit is wrong.

Limits. Scan time: 15.5 s (only `scan` spends it). Tool calls: 40 (every call counts once unless rejected). Rejected calls: 8 (a call refused for how it is written: unknown name, wrong type; costs nothing else), of them at most 3 refused `submit` calls. The episode ends at `submit` or at a limit; without `submit` the score is 0.
[scan time left 15.50 of 15.5 s · calls 0/40 · rejected 0/8]
~~~

## Determinism and versions

same (seed, level, tool calls) -> same observations, log hash chain and reward; a repeated scan draws new noise; the verifier's re-scan is noise-free.

Rewards are comparable only within one environment version (the `-vN` suffix) and one scanner engine (`mrgym --version`).
